title: Seattle Trivia Night

questions.q: The Space Needle was built for which event?
Seattle's nickname, the "_____ City", comes from which gemstone?
At which Seattle market do the fishmongers famously throw fish to one another?
Which guitarist, born in Seattle in 1942, recorded "Purple Haze"?
Which snow-capped volcano can be seen southeast of Seattle on a clear day?
Nirvana, Pearl Jam and Soundgarden are associated with which music genre that came out of the Seattle scene?
Which TV sitcom's title character was a psychiatrist with a radio call-in show in Seattle?
The Fremont Troll sculpture crouches under the north end of which bridge?
Seattle lies between Lake Washington and which inlet of the Pacific Ocean?
What is the name of Seattle's Major League Baseball team?

notes: Built for the Century 21 Exposition (the 1962 Seattle World's Fair); see the Space Needle's own history page or Wikipedia.
Official nickname 'The Emerald City', chosen through a tourism contest in the early 1980s; see Seattle (Wikipedia) or HistoryLink.org.
Fish throwing at Pike Place Fish Market inside Pike Place Market; see pikeplacemarket.org or Pike Place Fish Market (Wikipedia).
Hendrix was born in Seattle on 27 November 1942; 'Purple Haze' released 1967; see Jimi Hendrix (Wikipedia) or HistoryLink.org.
Mount Rainier lies about 60 miles southeast of Seattle; see the National Park Service Mount Rainier pages.
Grunge; see Grunge (Wikipedia) or the Museum of Pop Culture (MoPOP). Nirvana formed in Aberdeen but is part of the Seattle scene.
Frasier (NBC, 1993-2004): Dr Frasier Crane hosts a KACL radio show in Seattle; see Frasier (Wikipedia).
Fremont Troll, under the north end of the George Washington Memorial (Aurora) Bridge, 1990; see Fremont Troll (Wikipedia). Accept either bridge name.
Puget Sound; reworded so Elliott Bay (part of the Sound) is no longer a rival answer.
Seattle Mariners, MLB since 1977; see MLB.com or Seattle Mariners (Wikipedia).
